breaking_changes: The FastFlowLM NPU model hy-mt2:1.8b was renamed to hy-mt2-flash:1.8b in the upstream v1.0.7 release; update any configs or scripts that reference the old hy-mt2:1.8b tag.
The release tagging tool no longer accepts the --no-sign flag (omitting the flag now creates unsigned annotated tags by default); use --sign if you want a signed tag.

checklist.author: @abn
checklist.text: On a Linux or macOS desktop without lemond running, launch lemonade-tray with --spawn-server and verify that lemond starts within 15 seconds, the tray menu populates, and quitting the tray causes lemond to terminate immediately without leaving an orphan process.

checklist.author: @RaulMermans
checklist.text: Run lemonade config set flm.flm_bin=builtin and confirm it returns an Unknown key error, then run lemonade config set flm.npu_bin=builtin and confirm it succeeds.

checklist.author: @bitgamma
checklist.text: Start the Lemonade server on a Windows system with an AMD ROCm GPU, set the thenoise backend to rocm, and generate an image to confirm the bundled Python interpreter launches and produces output.

checklist.author: @ramkrishna2910
checklist.text: On Windows, connect to a server using an internal or private CA certificate (not a public CA like Let's Encrypt) and confirm the HTTPS connection succeeds without SSL connect errors.

checklist.author: @jeremyfowers
checklist.text: Start the server on macOS with extra_models_dir set to a directory containing nested subfolders, write a model file into one subfolder, and confirm the server's model list updates within a few seconds without any external trigger.

checklist.author: @julianxhokaxhiu
checklist.text: On a machine with an NPU, install this release and confirm that lemonade can discover and serve the hy-mt2-flash:1.8b model by name.

checklist.author: @jeremyfowers
checklist.text: Start the server, configure a very long global_timeout, and download a large model from a slow or flaky endpoint to confirm the download does not abort prematurely at 60 seconds but respects the global_timeout value.

checklist.author: @jeremyfowers
checklist.text: Start the server with extra_models_dir pointing at a Hugging Face cache that has two snapshots, set refs/main to the first, confirm the model lists as <repo> and <repo>-<quant>, then rename refs/main to the second snapshot and confirm the model name <repo> now resolves to the new checkpoint while the old snapshot is listed as <old-commit>-<repo>.

checklist.author: @jeremyfowers
checklist.text: Set extra_models_dir to a Hugging Face cache with two different orgs shipping the same repo name, confirm the first org's models list as <repo> and the second's as <org>-<repo>, then swap the directory listing order and confirm the names stay the same (org qualification, not discovery order).

checklist.author: @jeremyfowers
checklist.text: Set extra_models_dir to a cache whose GGUFs are in a subfolder like Q4_K_M/, confirm the model name is <repo>-Q4_K_M, then request that model by name to confirm it loads correctly.

checklist.author: @github-actions[bot]
checklist.text: Start the server with vulkan, rocm-stable, or rocm-nightly backend and load one model using each new architecture (clef, glm5-next, hrm_text, hy_v4, maple, spark2_5) to confirm it loads and answers without error.

checklist.author: @Copilot
checklist.text: Run the release tagging tool in dry-run mode and confirm the output says 'would create and push annotated tag' rather than 'signed tag'.

checklist.author: @Copilot
checklist.text: Run the release tagging tool with the --sign flag in dry-run mode and confirm the output says 'would create and push signed tag'.

checklist.author: @julianxhokaxhiu
checklist.text: Verify that any existing model registrations using the old hy-mt2:1.8b tag fail gracefully or produce a clear error, since the upstream binary no longer recognises that identifier.

evidence.blockers: No blocking P0 items. The most critical checks are the Windows internal CA HTTPS fix (b3cf539-1), which is a user-facing fix on a specific configuration, and the FLM model rename (8963505-1), which affects NPU users. The remaining 12 to-dos are P1/P2 and can be tested in parallel.
evidence.breaking_changes: The FastFlowLM NPU model hy-mt2:1.8b was renamed to hy-mt2-flash:1.8b in the upstream v1.0.7 release; update any configs or scripts that reference the old hy-mt2:1.8b tag. The release tagging tool's --no-sign flag was removed; omit the flag for unsigned tags or pass --sign for signed tags.
evidence.coverage: 31 commits reviewed across the range v2026.40.0..aa085f9, covering backends, CLI, config validation, tray subprocess management, downloads, extra_models_dir, HF/MS cache naming, model catalog, TLS, DirectoryWatcher, and release tooling. The release tagging tool's default-tag behavior was tested via dry-run only; no live tag was created in CI. Several new user-facing features (tray spawn, Windows ROCm TheNoise, HF cache naming, six new model architectures) lack automated end-to-end tests on target hardware.
evidence.manual_testing: A Windows tester with an internal/private CA must verify HTTPS connections succeed (b3cf539-1). An NPU user must verify the renamed hy-mt2-flash:1.8b model loads (8963505-1) and that old registrations produce a clear error (8963505-2). A Linux desktop tester should verify the tray --spawn-server lifecycle (3b5ec50-1). A macOS tester should verify nested extra_models_dir watches update automatically (b01156f-1). A Windows ROCm tester should verify TheNoise spawning (40827a3-1). A tester on any platform should verify download stall timeouts respect global_timeout (7dc09e2-1). A tester with an HF cache should verify refs/main switching (e4bcbd6-1). A tester should verify new model architectures load on vulkan/rocm backends (aa085f9-1). The release tagging tool dry-run flags (6deeb05-1, 6deeb05-2) are for release admins.
evidence.security: The curl CURLSSLOPT_REVOKE_BEST_EFFORT change on Windows (b3cf539) relaxes certificate revocation checking when CRL/OCSP responders are unreachable, enabling internal-CA connections but potentially allowing a revoked certificate from such a CA to be used in a targeted MITM attack. The posix_spawn watchdog in lemonade-tray (3b5ec50) uses FD_CLOEXEC and pipe-EOF for clean subprocess termination with no injection surface. The config validation tightening (a2e042d) is a defensive improvement.
